name: 2012 March Storm

phenomena.details: X5.4 flare on March 7, 2012 from AR 11429, followed by an X1.3 flare the same day.
Strong G3 geomagnetic storm with Dst ~ −131 nT (WDC Kyoto) on March 9.
Strong SEP event with >10 MeV proton flux exceeding 6000 pfu.

impacts.description: R3 radio blackouts from the X5.4 flare; HF communications disrupted across the sunlit hemisphere.
Elevated radiation environment from the SEP event; satellite operators reported increased anomaly rates.
FAA issued radiation advisory; some polar flights were rerouted to lower latitudes.
Aurora observed at mid-latitudes in North America and Europe during the G3 storm phase.

papers.title: THE MAJOR GEOEFFECTIVE SOLAR ERUPTIONS OF 2012 MARCH 7: COMPREHENSIVE SUN-TO-EARTH ANALYSIS
papers.authors: Patsourakos, S., Georgoulis, M. K., Vourlidas, A., et al.
papers.keyFinding: Comprehensive Sun-to-Earth analysis of the 7 March 2012 eruptions from AR 11429 and the resulting geomagnetic storm.

summary: The March 2012 storm, driven by an X5.4 flare from AR 11429 and a fast CME, produced a G3 storm (Dst ~ −131 nT) with a significant SEP event (>6000 pfu), causing radio blackouts, aviation radiation alerts, and aurora at mid-latitudes.
description: On March 7, 2012, AR 11429 produced an X5.4 flare followed closely by an X1.3 flare, launching fast Earth-directed CMEs. The resulting geomagnetic storm on March 9 reached G3 level with Dst ~ −131 nT and Kp 7. A significant SEP event produced >10 MeV proton flux exceeding 6,500 pfu, prompting the FAA to issue radiation advisories and airlines to reroute some polar flights. HF radio communications were severely disrupted. The event was extensively observed by SDO and other heliophysics spacecraft, providing rich multi-point data. This was one of the strongest events of Solar Cycle 24's ascending phase and demonstrated that even a relatively weak solar cycle could produce significant compound space weather events.
